newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end sharply down on comments about economy.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end sharply down on comments about economy.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended sharply lower on Wednesday, due to comments by senior government officials that recent rises in yen bond prices were not in line with the performance of the economy.

"Looking at yen bond futures, the upward trend is still in place, though the excessive rally has somewhat subsided. There is a clear discrepancy between the economic reality and the trend in the yen bond market," one official told Reuters.
The December ended at 124.85, down from Tuesday's 125.47.
"The (governor's) comments were not strong enough to have any effect," a trader for a city bank's securities affiliate said.
A city bank trader said there was little effect on JGBs since the BOJ governor's stance on the central bank's monetary policy seemed to be unchanged.
"The BOJ's monetary policy is geared to ensuring a firm basis for economic recovery," Matsushita said.
Asked if the BOJ intended to continue outright purchases of JGBs, Matsushita said the BOJ would continue to watch if such purchases were needed in light of the money supply.
Traders said the December fell sharply in the afternoon, due to comments from the officials.
"Bullish comments about the economy by senior government officials caused the fall," a trust bank trader said.

Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday afternoon that Japan's economy is recovering gradually, with private consumption resuming a gradual recovery after being somewhat sluggish in the summer.
Traders said Matsushita's comments, which came after the close of JGB futures trade, had little effect on cash JGBs.
The benchmark 182nd cash JGB yield stood at 2.620 percent as of 0726 GMT, up from Tuesday's 2.570 percent.
The benchmark yield had stood at 2.615 percent before the BOJ governor's news conference.

The market is now focusing its attention on the BOJ's key "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment due next Wednesday and a ten-year JGB auction, which is likely to take place next Tuesday, traders said.
Under current market conditions, the ten-year bonds are likely to be offered with a coupon of 2.8 percent or 2.7 percent, which are unlikely to attract investors, they said.
